proposed_features.description: Age ranges may correlate with income levels, with younger individuals typically earning less and older individuals potentially earning more due to experience or career progression.
Higher education levels (e.g., Bachelors, Prof-school) are associated with higher earning potential compared to lower levels (e.g., HS-grad).
Government or self-employed roles may differ in income potential compared to private sector jobs, with government roles sometimes offering stable but moderate pay.
Occupations like Prof-specialty or Exec-managerial tend to be higher-paying compared to Sales or Other-service.
Marital status may influence income, with married individuals sometimes earning more due to dual incomes or career stability.
Higher weekly hours may correlate with higher income, especially if combined with higher-paying occupations.
Presence of capital gain suggests investment income or asset appreciation, which may indicate higher overall income.
The size of capital gain can be a strong indicator of wealth or investment activity, with larger gains associated with higher income.
Relationship status (e.g., Husband, Own-child) may reflect household structure and income responsibilities, influencing reported income.
Gender may influence income due to historical wage gaps or occupational segregation.
Race may correlate with income due to socioeconomic factors, historical disparities, or access to opportunities.
Being native to the United-States may correlate with higher income due to access to better education, job markets, or longer residency.
